born.why: The code prioritizes survival by starving-override eating, avoids confirmed poisons, eats known safe fruits, tastes unknowns to gather data when safe, and only takes calculated risks on unknowns when hunger is critical.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when starvation is imminent, avoids poisonous fruits by checking the diary for past harm, uses 'taste' to safely identify new fruit species, and carries known safe food when hunger is manageable to preserve options.

The code improves safety by strictly avoiding species with a higher count of poisonous experiences than safe ones, while still allowing cautious exploration (tasting) of unknown or mixed-species fruits when hunger is high enough to justify the risk, ensuring survival without unnecessary starvation.

The code adjusts the thresholds for tasting and seeking unknown fruits to be more cautious, reducing the risk of poisoning while still allowing foraging when hungry. It retains the core logic of avoiding definitively poisonous fruits and leveraging known safe ones, ensuring a balance between survival and efficient foraging.

The code improves upon the original by handling ambiguous species through trait-based inference from other known safe/unsafe fruits, reducing unnecessary tasting of similar-looking but potentially safe items, and prioritizing carrying only when the fruit is explicitly targeted to optimize foraging efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by eating only when starving or if the fruit is a known target/high-hunger priority, uses a stricter poison-avoidance threshold (2x harm ratio) to prevent false negatives on new toxins, and defaults to tasting unknown fruits only when safe from starvation to accumulate necessary data for long-term survival.
